title: The point transport along Frobenius is linear and natural
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$, $n\geq1$, $s=\Spec k$ and $g_s=\Spec(\operatorname{Frob}_q):s\to s$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Let $\sigma_N$ and $\iota_N$ be the maps of the point transport [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], $\kappa_N$ and $c_\Lambda$ the comparison morphism and structure isomorphism of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] for $g=g_s$, $Lg_s^*$ the derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ the point fiber functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Then:

1. For $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E\}$ and every complex $N$ of $\Lambda_s$-modules on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], $\sigma_N:\Gamma(s,N)\to\Gamma(s,g_s^{-1}N)$ is $\Lambda$-linear, $\Lambda$ acting on $\Gamma(s,N)$ through $\Lambda\to\Gamma(s,\Lambda_s)$ and on $\Gamma(s,g_s^{-1}N)$ through $\Lambda\to\Gamma(s,\Lambda_s)$ and $c_\Lambda^{-1}$; $\sigma_N$ is natural in morphisms of complexes $N\to N'$; hence, $\Gamma(s,-)$ [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] and $g_s^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] being exact, the $\sigma_N$ define a natural transformation $\Gamma(s,-)\to\Gamma(s,g_s^{-1}(-))$ of functors $D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)\to D(\Lambda)$.

2. For each $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$ the morphisms $\iota_N$, $N\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], form a natural transformation $\iota:\operatorname{Fib}_s\to\operatorname{Fib}_s\circ Lg_s^*$ of functors on $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$: for every morphism $u:N\to N'$ of $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$, $\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*u)\circ\iota_N=\iota_{N'}\circ\operatorname{Fib}_s(u)$. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$ this includes the compatibility of $\iota^{E'}$ with the scalar extensions $E'\subset L$, under the isomorphisms $\operatorname{Fib}_s(K\otimes_{E'}L)\cong\operatorname{Fib}_s(K)\otimes_{E'}L$ of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] and $(Lg_{s,E'}^*K)\otimes_{E'}L\cong Lg_{s,L}^*(K\otimes_{E'}L)$ of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural] with $g=g_s$. Its restriction/coprojection is exactly $\sigma$ of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]; hence it gives clause (1), including all ambient derived morphisms.

The normalized comparison and common-stage realization assertions are agent-written, not theorems asserted by Deligne.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-natural] to $g_s$: this is a scheme isomorphism and $\ell\ne p$ is invertible on $s$. Its composition assertion, with $S=H=\Gamma(s,-)$ and $\rho=\sigma$ from Step 1, makes $\Gamma(\kappa)\sigma$ natural. By [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] restrict to the finite and completed integral constructible categories. Since the fiber functors there are sections [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and $\iota=\Gamma(\kappa)\sigma$ [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], this is clause (2) at these stages.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-point-automorphism-transport-scalar-extension] with $g=g_s$. Its $t^E=\Gamma(\kappa^E)\sigma^{g,E}$ equals the integral $\iota$ [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. It supplies exactly the scalar-compatibility hypothesis of [lem-weil-point-transformation-coefficient-descent] for this family. Its rational equation also gives the scalar-extension clause of (2), with the specified sections comparison [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] and pullback comparison [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension].

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-point-transformation-coefficient-descent] with $\eta^E=\iota^{\mathcal O_E}$ for every finite coefficient field $E$: Step 2 gives its integral naturality and Step 3 its coefficient compatibility. Its two conclusions give naturality for every rational morphism and every common-stage morphism. The components are precisely the tensor-extended and stage-represented components specified by [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. This finishes clause (2) for $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q97-b557d6fc3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: This delivery fulfils the re-split note. The previous Q97 head 473e43d1 was RETURNed (G1/D) because old steps 3–5 and 6/9 stayed inline. This head adds two new statement-only nodes for exactly those arguments and keeps the two earlier nodes byte-identical; the earlier review judged both true, and I agree. Compared with live, the statement, stmt_deps and Lean record are unchanged and no parallel group has superseded the item. The proof is 4 steps, 1809 characters; the four nodes are 2318, 2382, 2743 and 3387 characters, none restating the item. Every old step maps to a node: 1–2 restriction, 3–5 κ-naturality, 7–8 scalar square, 6 and 9 descent. (1) lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-natural is true. The finite κ is the class of x↦x⊗1 (def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison (a)), natural on chain maps and on inverted quasi-isomorphisms. For the integral κ, the normalization node gives a natural θ with θκ = G(u), so P(v)κ_N = θ'^{-1}G(v̂)G(u_N) = κ_{N'}G(v); this also holds for incomplete N, and no invertibility is claimed (g = id gives the completion unit). The ρ-composition clause is formal. No existing node states naturality of the specified κ: I read the grep hits for def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison, including trf tower-unit, resolution-matching, reduction-counit and pod canonical-coefficient. (2) lem-weil-point-transformation-coefficient-descent is true. Rational sums follow from Fib(f⊗λ) = λ(Γf⊗E) and Lf^*(u⊗c) = Lf^*u⊗c. The Q̄ action formulas match def-weil-finite-coefficient-point item 4 (conjugation by φ̄) and def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom (conjugation by θ^{f*} = ᾱ), so b = φ̄F(ᾱ)^{-1}. The rationalized hypothesis puts the components at a common stage, and equality in the Hom colimit (def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category) gives representative independence. Components match def-weil-frobenius-point-transport (ι^E = ι^{O_E}⊗E, Q̄ represented at E'). Assembly: step 1 is the restriction node at g_s (same coprojection). Step 2 takes S = H = Γ and ρ = σ, then restricts via lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback. In step 3 the scalar node's t-equation is literally the descent hypothesis, and its rational form is the scalar clause of (2). Step 4 applies descent. stmt_deps match the statement citations exactly, and proof_deps equal the union of the steps' uses. Dropped proof_deps are still cited by other nodes, so none is orphaned. Batch-5 flags accepted: both route to lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization. It is a coefficient-foundation identification (specified inverse-image map = completion unit), not the trace formula, Poincaré duality or a step of their proofs. The base item already cited it, so the batch-5 closure gains nothing. No SGA citation. No fixes.
